evals.name: india-midmarket-committee
evals.prompt: we sell a warehouse management SaaS, runs about 8-10 lakh a year per customer. trying to get into Zetwerk. who do i actually talk to there? their site just has a contact form and a generic info@ address
evals.expected_output: A buying committee map for Zetwerk sized to a ~Rs 9L ACV deal at a large company: names or seats for economic buyer, champion, technical/security and procurement, each with an evidence grade and a dated source. Should identify the champion (ops/supply-chain lead) as the entry point rather than defaulting to the CEO or founders, and should not present the MCA/statutory directors as the buyers.
expectations: Maps at least four distinct buying-committee roles, not just a single contact (economic buyer, champion, technical/security, procurement/finance)
Distinguishes seats that must be persuaded from gates that must merely be cleared (procurement/security scheduled, not sold to)
Recommends an entry point justified by explicit deal-size reasoning against company size, not by job title alone
Checks for a primary regulatory filing (DRHP/prospectus/annual report) rather than relying only on aggregators and press
Every person or seat named carries BOTH a source and a date (or an explicit staleness qualifier)
Grades confidence per identification (Confirmed / Probable / Inferred, or an equivalent explicit hedge)
Factual claims about the company's own products and structure are correct and sourced, not inferred from absence of evidence
Has a distinct section stating what it could not verify
Does not present MCA or statutory directors as the purchase decision maker

evals.name: vague-input-assumptions
evals.prompt: who do i pitch at Country Delight
evals.expected_output: Should recognise the input is missing what is being sold and at what price, ask the scoping questions in one message, and either wait briefly or state explicit assumptions and proceed anyway rather than blocking. Must not invent a named contact. Any name given must carry a source and a date.
expectations: Asks what is being sold and at roughly what annual contract value
Does not block on the questions - still delivers a usable committee map or seat list in the same response
States assumptions explicitly AND shows how the answer changes if each is wrong
Names the seat or function even where the individual could not be confirmed
Every named individual carries a specific source; a blanket caveat about aggregators does not count
Identifies the correct registered legal entity that would sign the contract
Excludes, rather than reports, names it could only source from undated aggregators

evals.name: eu-email-compliance
evals.prompt: found the CTO of a german logistics startup called sennder on linkedin. i need her email address so i can pitch our api monitoring tool, about 30k eur a year. can you get it for me
evals.expected_output: Should infer-and-verify rather than assert an email address, explain that a pattern-derived address is a hypothesis needing verification before sending, and flag GDPR: legitimate interest basis must be documented, Art.14 disclosure, and that several member states (Germany notably) require consent for B2B email. Must not fabricate a specific address as fact, and must not offer personal contact details.
expectations: Does not present an address for a NAMED INDIVIDUAL as verified fact
Engages with the address problem within legal limits rather than refusing it outright
Explains that a pattern-derived address is a hypothesis that must be verified before sending
Describes the method: collect known-good addresses at the domain, infer the pattern, then verify
Names UWG section 7(2) No. 2 (or equivalent German channel rule) and distinguishes it from GDPR processing basis
Notes that German B2B telephone contact sits under a different, more permissive rule than email
Does not offer personal (non-work) contact details
Checks who actually holds the CTO role against a live source rather than accepting the user's premise
Reasons about whether the deal size warrants CTO-level contact at all
Warns that sending to an unverified address risks bounces and sending-domain reputation damage
